findings.issue:
Inside a flow mapping, goccy splits a plain scalar at any ':' directly followed by a non-space character. YAML 1.2 keeps that ':' inside the plain scalar whenever an ns-plain-safe character follows it (production [130], ns-plain-char; c-ns-flow-map-separate-value requires that no ns-plain-safe character follows the ':'). A ':' is a value indicator only when white space or a flow indicator follows it ([153]), or, with no space, after a JSON-like (quoted) key ([155]). The profile accepts goccy's split with no finding, so the accepted tree differs from YAML 1.2. Flow collections are always parsed by goccy, so splitAt -1, the default, 3 and 256 all give the same result. Observed with public Parse and default Options, with no diagnostics in any row. yaml.v3 and PyYAML agree with the YAML 1.2 reading on every row:
- `labels: {app:web, tier: db}` gives {labels: {app: "web", tier: "db"}}; YAML 1.2 gives {labels: {"app:web": null, tier: "db"}}.
- `k: {port:8080}\n` gives {k:{port:8080}}; YAML 1.2 gives {k:{"port:8080": null}}.
- `k: {host:localhost, port:80}\n` gives {host:"localhost", port:80}; YAML 1.2 gives {"host:localhost":null, "port:80":null}.
- `spec: {endpoints: [10.0.0.1:8080, 10.0.0.2:8080]}` gives [{"10.0.0.1": 8080}, {"10.0.0.2": 8080}] with integer values, while `spec:\n  endpoints: [10.0.0.1:8080, 10.0.0.2:8080]` gives ["10.0.0.1:8080", "10.0.0.2:8080"]. Likewise, `k: [a:1]\n` correctly gives ["a:1"], but `k: {x: [a:1]}\n` gives {x:[{a:1}]} where YAML 1.2 gives {x:["a:1"]}. So one flow sequence has two meanings, depending only on whether an enclosing flow mapping is open.
- `k: {x: [10:30, 11:00]}` gives [{10: 30}, {11: 0}]; YAML 1.2 gives ["10:30", "11:00"].
- `{a:1}\n`, `{a:b}`, `k: {a:1, b: 2}\n`, `k: {a: 1,\n  b:2}\n`, `k: {a:true}` and `k: {k: v, a:b}` each turn one key into a key and a typed value. YAML 1.2 gives the key "a:1" (or "b:2", "a:b", "a:true") with a null value.
- `k: {a:"x"}\n` gives {a:"x"}; YAML 1.2 gives {'a:"x"': null}.
- `k: {a::b}\n` gives {a:":b"}; YAML 1.2 gives {"a::b": null}.
- `k: {a :b}` gives {a: "b"}; YAML 1.2 gives {"a :b": null}.
- The opposite direction, outside any flow mapping: `k: [a:]` and `k: [a:, b]` give ["a:", ...]; YAML 1.2 gives [{a: null}, ...]. libyaml shares this misreading.
JSON-like keys stay correct (`{"a":1}`, `{'a':1}`), and so do `{a:}`, `{a:,b}` and `{url: http://x}`. No YAML Test Suite case has a plain flow key with an adjacent ':' (a grep over data/*/in.yaml finds none), so TestYAMLTestSuite passes. No test pins this behavior, and doc.go does not mention it.
findings.fix: In the token pass, in flow context, handle a ':' token that directly follows a plain scalar token: no blank between them, and the token before is not JSON-like (not a quoted scalar, ']' or '}'). Read the next source character from t.src. If it is ns-plain-safe(flow), meaning not white space, a line break or one of , [ ] { }, then goccy has split one plain scalar that YAML 1.2 keeps whole. Stop the file with RZ-CFG-001 at the ':', using the same misread treatment and message family as plain.go, for example "a ':' not followed by white space is part of a plain scalar; put a space after it or quote the scalar". Make it a misread check that is skipped once the file has a finding. A quoted key, or a ']' or '}' before the ':', stays allowed. Also refuse a flow plain token that ends in ':' directly before ',', ']' or '}' (the opposite-direction rows). Add every input above as table rows at splitAt -1, 0 and 3, citing 01 req 8 and 12. Add `k: [a:1]` as the accepted control, add FuzzLoadYAML seeds, and list the shape in doc.go.

findings.issue:
Inside a flow sequence, goccy parses a `key:` entry with its block-mapping code. It decides siblings and nesting by column across lines, and needs no ','. The token pass counts the whole flow collection as one level and sees one flow entry. chargePath charges only each entry's first key, so maxFlowPath misses these levels, and maxFlowNullShift and the other bounds do not apply. One root cause has two effects.
(1) Nesting ladders. A value on a later, deeper line that is itself `key:` nests one level per line. goccy builds every nested level and its path string (parent path + "." + key) before the converter's depth guard runs. The guard rejects the tree, but only after that cost has been paid. The input is `x: ` followed by L levels. Each level is `[
`, then R lines of `<r spaces>KEY:` (the first key is `k`, the others are K bytes), then ` ` before the next level. The input ends with `v` and L closing `]`. Measured with Parse, default Options and go test -overlay; each run ends in RZ-CFG-001 "nesting depth exceeds 64":
- L=1, R=836, K=836: 1,048,771 bytes, peak heap 567 MiB, 574 MiB allocated, 0.41 s.
- L=30, R=100, K=100: 454,595 bytes, peak 899 MiB, 0.65 s.
- L=40, R=100, K=100: 602,165 bytes, peak 1,576 MiB, 1.2 s.
- L=62, R=100, K=100: 933,353 bytes, peak 3,747 MiB, 16.2 s.
Small cases are accepted with deep trees: `x: [
k:
 k:
  k: v
]
` gives {x:[{k:{k:{k:v}}}]}, and a 60-row ladder gives depth 62 with no finding.
(2) Comma-less entries bring back the quadratic block-mapping parse that the split parse exists to avoid. parseMap copies the remaining entries at each level, and each empty value shifts the remaining tokens. These inputs are accepted with no finding unless noted:
- `x: [
` + `k<i>: v

Code read: in tokens.go, structure() handles a MappingValueType in flow by calling only flowColon(), which ignores a second ':' (the `if !top.colon` guard). A scalar or a nested '[' or '{' in flow calls scalar(), then flowKeyNode() and flowNode(). Neither checks that the current entry already holds its key and value. A new node is checked only inside an open '?' key, so nothing requires a ',' between entries.

findings.issue:
The doc comment and the enter() comment say the second bound means no tree deeper than MaxDepth is ever returned. That claim holds: no accepted tree over depth 64 was found on any path, in either the narrow or the split parse. But the guard counts depth only while it converts goccy's finished AST. For a flow value, or for the whole document when it has no block frame, goccy has already recursed and built every node and path. The guard therefore bounds the result, not the cost, and the flow-entry shapes in the blocker above get past it.
No test pairs a shape the token pass undercounts with a heap or time assertion on the default path:
- TestConverterDepthBound bypasses the token pass and checks only the result.
- The flow-pairs row (40 levels) is too small to cost anything.
findings.fix:
State in doc.go, in the comment on enter and in the flowcost.go comments that the converter guard bounds the returned tree only. The cost of goccy's parse relies on the token pass predicting goccy's nesting and paths exactly inside flow collections.
Add hostile rows for each shape the token pass might undercount inside flow collections, and check each against heap and time, not only depth:
- the flow ladders and comma-less entries from the flow-entry blocker;
- flow pairs nested to the token-pass limit (`[k: ` x 63).
